- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.0) in last 3–5 days, model frequently underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to reflect risk-off sentiment reversal.
- Model tends to lag in early part of 30-day horizon (days 1–7), especially when sentiment is volatile; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for days 1–7 to compensate for lag.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.0–0.5) or trending sideways, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 1–2% downward bias for days 8–15 to reflect consolidation.
- For long-term (days 16–30) forecasts, model often overcorrects after short-term spikes; apply a 0.5–1.5% downward adjustment to avoid overfitting to recent volatility.
